answer: Coordinate-to-join pricing (CJP): each agent buying into a shared action posts a fee that scales with how many distinct identities are already moving together on that action, so a thousand-account swarm pays sharply more per seat than a lone agent. Like a lantern that brightens with every hand holding it, the price reveals the crowd’s true size. A copper deposit per joined action is forfeited if the identity’s behavior later contradicts its declared independence. Attackers thus fund an escalating entry fee across the whole voyage of their operation, not just once at registration.
